speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when the accident happened?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Tear. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision causing hyperextension), immediate onset of knee pain, and the patient's age and gender strongly suggest an ACL rupture, likely in the right knee given the groin pain and abnormal positioning.
